claim: Envoy's ext_proc filter exposes a failure_mode_allowed counter that tracks the number of times an ext_proc gRPC error was ignored due to configuration, making fail-open behavior observable at the Envoy telemetry layer.
stance_target: mechanisms for detecting/configuring fail-open behavior when an EPP is unreachable
scope_conditions: Envoy ext_proc HTTP filter, current docs
quoted_support: failure_mode_allowed | Counter | The number of times an error was ignored due to configuration

claim: The ext_proc filter protocol is a bidirectional gRPC stream in which the external processor (e.g., EPP) can mutate headers, body, and trailers, or return an entirely new response, on a message-by-message basis.
stance_target: mechanism by which EPP communicates routing decisions to the gateway
quoted_support: The processing service itself implements a gRPC interface that allows it to respond to events in the lifecycle of an HTTP request / response by examining and modifying the headers, body, and trailers of each message, or by returning a brand-new response.
